frequency_question: How often do proposed regulatory capital buffer increases successfully complete the necessary administrative procedural steps and take effect within a 92-day or similar short-duration horizon?
membership_rule: Includes any formal regulatory action by the Federal Reserve to adjust the countercyclical capital buffer or equivalent macroprudential capital requirements through notice and comment rulemaking.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named major capital framework procedural implementations analyzed for duration constraints.
known_gaps: Short-window emergency interim final rules exist but standard CCyB adjustments require full notice and comment.
skeleton: Regulatory rulemakings completed by the Federal Reserve Board of Governors meeting administrative Procedure Act requirements.
multiplier: Standard rulemaking timeline: Proposal drafting (2-4 months) + Public comment period (60-90 days) + Review and final rule formulation (3-6 months) = Minimum 6 to 12 months for any substantive capital buffer adjustment.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act timelines and Federal Reserve internal clearance procedures remain stable over multi-year horizons.
